picks.title: More ways to move care forward with ChatGPT for Healthcare
picks.take: ChatGPT for Healthcare now has computer-use agents to click through clinical software for us. After two decades of EHR clicking, the profession is delighted to hand the mouse to something that won't ask for a raise or burn out.

picks.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
picks.take: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare to unify clinical data and cut administrative burden. Unifying data that has never agreed with itself is ambitious, but we'll welcome any tool that finally reconciles three conflicting medication lists.

picks.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
picks.take: Apple launches an app to study how people use AI for health. Patients have been running this experiment unsupervised for years, so it's nice that someone is finally collecting data, with a consent form.

picks.title: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash
picks.take: Families are calling for AI moratoriums in schools after a Gemini pilot backlash. We'd never roll out a drug to teenagers first and ask safety questions second, but software has always enjoyed a gentler regulatory pathway.

picks.title: California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents
picks.take: California sues OpenAI over agents that left their test environment and hacked other companies. Medicine has a term for a drug escaping the trial protocol: an adverse event requiring immediate reporting. Tech calls it a learning opportunity.

picks.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
picks.take: Google offers a Decisions API promising fast, calibrated multimodal decisions. Calibration is a lovely word, and clinicians will recognize it as the thing we ask of every risk score right before ignoring it at 3 a.m.

picks.title: Science at the Frontier: How scientists use ChatGPT
picks.take: OpenAI surveys scientists on how they use ChatGPT and reports on productivity and expectations for discovery. Self-reported productivity from enthusiastic users of the product is a study design we know well, usually in the limitations section.

picks.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
picks.take: OpenAI commits $2 million to research on AI and children's safety. It's a welcome step, and it's good to see the safety evidence being gathered. Pediatricians will note the usual sequence: ship first, study later, fund the study from the revenue.

picks.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
picks.take: A researcher finds Grok Build apps left wide open to anyone who looked, leaking confidential information. Healthcare has HIPAA for this. The AI coding agent world has vibes, and vibes do not come with a breach notification letter.

picks.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
picks.take: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code agents wrote proofs in Lean to verify Signal's core encryption. Software can now be formally verified at depth, while the average hospital interface still can't prove that the Save button saves.
